title: Maria Goretti (6 July)
hookLine: an eleven-year-old who forgave the young man who killed her; he later repented
tomorrow: Our Lady of Mount Carmel (16 July)

lines: WHAT SHE SAID BEFORE SHE DIED.
cards: A farmhouse in the Italian countryside, shared by two poor families. In one, a widow and her children; the oldest girl, Maria, minds the little ones while her mother works the fields.
In the other, a young man named Alessandro. One afternoon, when the house is nearly empty, he tries to force himself on her. She refuses him, and he stabs her.
She is carried to a hospital, and she does not live long. This is a hard story, and the Church tells it gently. It doesn't dwell on the attack.
It turns to something she said before she died.

teach.b: The Church's account says Maria Goretti was eleven. As she lay dying, she was asked about the young man who had hurt her, and the account says she forgave him and hoped to see him in heaven.
That's the whole of her teaching, one sentence from a child. Catholics hear in it an echo of the cross.
In the Douay-Rheims, Jesus says from the cross: "Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do." Then the story turns to Alessandro.
He goes to prison, and for a long time, by the account, he shows no sorrow at all. Then, tradition says, he sees Maria in a dream, offering him flowers. Something in him breaks open.

teach.h: A DREAM, A PRISON, A MOTHER.
teach.b: Years later, out of prison, he goes to Maria's mother and asks her forgiveness. She gives it. The story told about that day says the two of them went to Mass together and received communion side by side.

Afterward Alessandro lived out his life quietly among Capuchin friars, working as a gardener and a porter. Catholics honor Maria as a martyr, and her feast is kept on the sixth of July. One thing matters here.
Her forgiveness was her gift, freely given.

It isn't a rule laid on anyone who has been hurt, and it doesn't erase what was done. Catholic writers have said this carefully: forgiving is not pretending, and it never asks someone to stay in danger.
What her story holds out is something else: a wound that, in time, became a door for the person who caused it.

how: Catholics keep the memorial of Saint Maria Goretti on 6 July, and some parishes remember victims of violence in the prayers at Mass that day.

practice: Bring to mind people hurt by violence, near or far: a name from the news, a street in your own town, someone you know who never talks about it. Don't push for feelings; just keep them company for a while.
If you pray, pray for them, or say the Our Father slowly with them in mind; if you don't, hold them in your attention, one breath for each.

wordCard.voice: Maria Goretti. A young Italian girl who refused her attacker, forgave him before she died, and whose forgiveness reached him years later.

carryVoice: Your line: forgiveness at eleven. Her forgiveness was hers to give, and it reached further than anyone expected. Go gently.
